parts.name: green body shell

physics.Basic_description: Teal-green painted metal structure forming the base, fuel tank, and top chimney assembly with a matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Houses the fuel reservoir, supports the glass globe, and channels airflow for combustion.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the cylindrical base or the upper chimney section firmly with parallel jaws.
physics.reason: Standard lantern construction uses thin sheet metal for the body to minimize weight while containing fuel and air.

parts.name: globe glass

physics.Basic_description: Translucent white frosted glass cylinder situated centrally within the metal frame.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the flame from wind and diffuses the light emitted by the wick.
physics.Grasped_description: Avoid grasping directly due to fragility; if necessary, use soft fingertips with minimal force.
physics.reason: Glass globes are blown or molded shells with uniform wall thickness to withstand thermal stress.

parts.name: guard member 0

physics.Basic_description: Curved teal-green metal rods running vertically along the sides of the globe.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the glass globe from impact and provides structural support for the handle pivots.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the vertical rod section with parallel jaws, ensuring not to squeeze too hard against the glass.
physics.reason: Guard wires are typically solid metal rods bent into shape for rigidity.

parts.name: flame

physics.Basic_description: Orange glowing region inside the glass globe representing the fire.
physics.Functional_description: Source of light and heat generated by burning kerosene.
physics.Grasped_description: Cannot be grasped; intangible energy source.
physics.reason: A flame is a volume of gas/plasma with no solid walls, effectively hollow/empty in terms of material occupancy.

physics.reason: These are openings in the thin sheet metal shell of the chimney.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
